issues.title: Binary-shift endpoint
issues.failure_explanation: The maps b_ell and b_{ell+1} are defined on Z_{2^ell} and Z_{2^{ell+1}}, respectively. At the admitted endpoint k=2^ell-1, the third identity invokes b_ell(2^ell) and b_{ell+1}(2^{ell+1}), neither of which is defined. The special convention for dyadic grid-point notation does not extend the binary-representation maps themselves.
issues.overall_effect: Only the endpoint instance of the lemma's third auxiliary identity is ill-formed. The first two identities retain their full range, and the dyadic-refinement corollary and main correctness chain need only those valid identities or direct interval arithmetic.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State the first two binary-shift identities for 0 ≤ k ≤ 2^ℓ−1, but state b_{ℓ+1}(2k+2)=0 b_ℓ(k+1) only for 0 ≤ k ≤ 2^ℓ−2. The existing proof then applies on the well-defined range, and no downstream result requires alteration.
issues.why_classification: The declared domains of the binary maps uniquely force exclusion of the final endpoint: at k=2^ℓ−1 the third identity is not a coherent proposition because both displayed map evaluations are undefined. This is an off-by-one range transcription, with no mathematical inference or downstream guarantee requiring repair.

issues.title: Zero-mass angle assignment
issues.failure_explanation: The prose claims to define an angle in [0,pi/2], but when p_w=0 the displayed cases impose cos^2(theta_w)=0 and sin^2(theta_w)=0. Every real angle instead satisfies cos^2(theta_w)+sin^2(theta_w)=1. This case is admissible—for example, a normalized nonnegative density may vanish on an entire dyadic interval—so the angle family used by the proposition is not literally defined. The proposition's proof itself reveals the intended convention by setting theta_w=0.
issues.overall_effect: For allowed densities having a zero-mass dyadic branch, the literal angle family and hence the stated factorization and circuit construction are not well-defined until a zero-mass convention is supplied. No restriction on the density or theorem is needed after the local correction.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Retain the ratio definitions when p_w>0 and, when p_w=0, define θ_w:=0 directly—equivalently, set cos²θ_w=1 and sin²θ_w=0. With that convention, the trigonometric factorization, inductive-state lemma, and state-preparation theorem remain unchanged.
issues.why_classification: The old proof explicitly states θ_w=0 on a zero-mass branch, uniquely fixing the intended reading of the malformed displayed cases. Thus the impossible pair cos²θ_w=sin²θ_w=0 is a transcriptional case-entry error; correcting it requires no new argument, restriction, or loss anywhere in the affected chain.

issues.title: Gray-code flip masks
issues.failure_explanation: With b_3^{-1}(z_1z_2z_3)=z_1+2z_2+4z_3, the Gray words have integer values 0,1,3,2,6,7,5,4. Their consecutive XORs are therefore (1,2,1,4,1,2,1), not (4,2,4,1,4,2,4), and the corresponding flip indices are (1,2,1,3,1,2,1), not (3,2,3,1,3,2,3).
issues.overall_effect: The labeled m=3 example reverses the first and third bit weights and would identify the wrong CNOT controls if its numerical lists were followed. The generic definitions and pseudocode compute the masks independently, so no formal result depends on the erroneous table.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Using the stated LSB-first encoding, record γ(k)=(0,1,3,2,6,7,5,4), replace the flip-mask list by (d_1,…,d_7)=(1,2,1,4,1,2,1), and replace the flip-index list by (j(1),…,j(7))=(1,2,1,3,1,2,1). No change to the generic Gray-code definitions or pseudocode is needed.
issues.why_classification: The repair is short, local, and preserves the example and all general constructions, with no formal result affected. It nevertheless requires recomputing the integer XOR masks and resulting control indices after the example applied the stated bit-weight convention incorrectly, so it is a genuine routine computational correction rather than a purely transcriptional typo.
